svg.title: Consigned cut tape: long strips, not short ones
svg.desc: Drawn to scale, 8 mm carrier tape seen from above, with a part in every pocket. Top: one continuous strip 240 mm long, with the round sprocket holes along the top and an arrow showing the direction of feed to the right (EIA-481), so the right-hand end goes into the feeder first; 50 mm is marked as the shortest strip that can be handled and 150 mm as the preferred minimum, and the parts at both ends are marked as the ones that may be lost. Bottom: the same kind of parts sent as five strips of ten, each 40 mm long, shorter than the 50 mm minimum.

g.text: Last part in: the trailing end
Usually no empty leader on cut tape
First part in: the leading end
May be lost; buy a little extra (attrition)
Each strip loaded or spliced by hand
Shorter than 50 mm: too short to load
Drawn to scale: 8 mm tape, 4 mm pitch.
Shortest strip: 50 mm minimum, 150 mm or more preferred
Feed direction per EIA-481: cover tape up, round sprocket
holes at the top, unreeling to the right.
